The Unistellar Envision smart binoculars have an augmented reality (AR) overlay that provides smart functionality to 10x50 binoculars, enabling night sky and landmark identification.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

I have been waiting to get my hands on a pair of Unistellar Envision smart binoculars since they were announced in 2024. Our editor-in-chief tried an early demo of them last year and said that they felt like something out of Star Trek. He was, of course, referencing the red augmented reality (AR) overlay in the Envisions that can identify night sky targets and landmarks, as well as displaying navigational tools. These are the first pair of smart binoculars that can identify targets in the night sky, such as planets, stars and deep space objects.

The build is solid and while they aren't the most lightweight binoculars, the body is hiding that extra technology that enables the AR overlay in the right hand lens. Each pair ships with a soft carry case, a padded neck strap, a USB-C cable and rubber caps for the eyepieces and lenses.

Pre-order the Unistellar Envision smart binoculars for $1,499 / £1,299

I would highly recommend setting these binoculars up in the daytime, as you definitely need a few minutes to get used to the controls and to perform the diopter adjustment. After powering on, all I had to do was connect the model to the Unistellar app, which recognised the device easily and then watch the onboarding videos. Unistellar also recommends performing a 360-degree calibration before your first use to help ensure the best performance.

You need to have location services set to "always" for the Unistellar app so that it can work out your exact location and give you an accurate reading on the augmented reality (AR) display for locations of night sky targets and landmarks.

I haven't had chance to use the night mode on these binoculars yet, thanks to cloudy skies, but I did use the topographical identification and was impressed with the ease of identifying landmarks around my local area. Besides the night and daytime modes, there is also a navigation mode which displays your cardinal direction alongside degrees of your azimuth and elevation angles.

I had a chance to try out the target lock feature on a geographical landmark with a friend and they found the target easily via the indicator on the AR display. The issue with swapping between two people is that the diopter adjustment only be accurate for one person and I can imagine that constantly changing it during field observation would be annoying. My friend also had to adjust the focus wheel to get the AR overlay sharp enough to read but it was a minor inconvenience.

The controls are intuitive and easy to use once you are used to the placement on the top panel. On the left you have the "next" button for advancing a guided tour to the next target, the "target lock" button and the "mode" button for cycling through the different display modes. On the right is the calibration button for adjusting the augmented reality (AR) display against your real-world view and the power button, which doubles up as a switch to turn the AR display on and off.

I'm looking forward to putting the Unistellar Envisions through their paces as I spend more time with them and get some clear skies to try them out on some stars. I think that these are going to be a great tool for learning my way around the night sky, as well as being invaluable when trying to teach others about constellations and targets. With extra functionality expected in future software updates and a plan to allow third-party app development in 2027, I am excited about the possibilities of the exciting new world of smart binoculars.

#869. Keira Knightley Reveals Which of Her Movies She’s Only Seen Once

Keira Knightley—who played Juliet in the 2003 film Love Actually—revealed she’s only seen the Christmas classic one time: “I think I’m the person that knows it the least of anybody.”

If you look for it, you'll find that Keira Knightley’s love for Love Actually isn’t, actually, all around.

After all, the 41-year-old—who played Juliet in the 2003 rom-com—revealed she’s only seen the film once.

“I have not watched Love Actually since the premiere, which was when I was 18,” she told Heart in a video shared Nov. 9. “So, I think I’m the person that knows it the least of anybody.”

And before you go asking her what could be worse than the total agony of being in love, just know there’s a high chance she’ll have no idea what you’re on about.

“I know that people have a particular look on their face and then they say things to me and I know that means they’re quoting Love Actually,” she explained, “but I don’t really know what it is. It means nothing to me.”

Plus, it doesn’t help that the Pirates of the Caribbean actress’ time on set was so short.

“It was a week when I was 17,” she noted. “So, I don’t remember it, really.”

Even so, she’s proud of the film’s legacy.

“I quite like that it has this life,” she added. “Such a big life out there.”

The Richard Curtis-directed Christmas classic follows a slew of interconnected love stories in London during the weeks leading up to the Dec. 25 holiday. And while some characters in the film get the s--t kicked out of them by love, Knightley’s Juliet finds herself in a love triangle with her husband Peter (Chiwetel Ejiofor) and his best friend Mark (Andrew Lincoln).

The situation comes to a head when Mark shows up on Christmas to profess his love using cue-cards. And while the scene has cemented itself as one of the most unforgettable rom-com moments in history, the Pride & Prejudice star previously revealed she and the film’s director worked hard to make sure the grand gesture didn’t seem "stalker-ish" for viewers.

“My memory is of Richard, who is now a very dear friend, of me doing the scene, and him going, ‘No, you’re looking at [Andrew] like he’s creepy,’" she told Variety in 2024. "And I’m like, ‘But it is quite creepy.’"

That’s why Knightley changed up her facial expression to try to improve the scene, recalling that she continued by “having to redo it to fix my face to make him seem not creepy.”

For more proof that Love Actually secrets really are all around, read on…

1. Love Actually opens with scenes of travelers hugging and kissing their nearest and dearest as they reunite at London's Heathrow Airport."This is my favorite bit in the film, in fact," writer/director Richard Curtis said in a director's commentary version of the film. "This footage was shot by a hidden camera, which was in Heathrow Airport for a whole week."And the movie's team really had to jet to get permission to use these clips of real-life passengers."Every time they saw something they really liked, then the runner would charge off and ask the people to sign a bit of paper, whether or not they were happy that it should be shown in the film," he continued. "I still think it'll be quite a surprise to the people who go to the cinema and see themselves."As for the inspiration behind the scene, it came from Curtis' personal experience."I got stuck in an airport in L.A. for an hour and a half waiting for a package, and I just saw all these people just all hugging and kissing," he added. "And you realize that behind normal people in the park and in the street, there's all these stories of love."

2. The first character fans meet in the 2003 movie is Bill Nighy's Billy Mack. He's a rock and roll star approaching his golden years who releases a holiday cover of Wet Wet Wet's "Love Is All Around," which secured the No. 1 spot in the U.K. for 15 weeks after the release of Curtis' 1994 film Four Weddings and a Funeral.While it can be hard to imagine anyone but Nighy playing the part, he wasn't initially in the running for the role. It wasn't until the actor stepped in to help with a table read that Curtis knew he was the one for the job."I had two famous guys in mind to play the aging rocker Billy Mack, and I couldn't decide who to ask," the filmmaker told The Guardian in 2013. "But at the read-through, Bill did it so perfectly he became a definite yes. I've never told anyone else who I wanted. I'll put it in my will."

3. Martin Freeman has also shared his casting story. In Love Actually, he portrays a man named John who meets a woman named Judy (Joanna Page) while they're stand-ins for a movie and filming a sex scene. They have great conversations, go out on a date and fall in love.At the time of casting, Curtis had fallen in love with the U.K. version of The Office, which Freeman starred on from 2001 to 2003."I got attached to Love Actually because on the back of The Office Richard Curtis wrote me a very nice and flattering letter that contained a piece of chocolate in it," The Hobbit star recalled to Vanity Fair in 2020. "It was like a wrapped chocolate presented to me saying, 'I love The Office. I love what you did in The Office. It was amazing.'"

4. Before Thomas Brodie-Sangster was cast as Sam—a British boy who loses his mom and turns to his stepdad Daniel (Liam Neeson) to help him navigate his crush on American schoolmate Joanna—Joe Alwyn tried out for the part."This local community center where I took fencing lessons, this brilliant U.K. casting director called Shaheen Baig, she came around and she saw me there," The Favourite alum and ex of Taylor Swift, shared on a 2018 episode of Live With Kelly and Ryan. "It meant that I got time off school to go to this audition, so I went to it."In fact, Alwyn said he went through several rounds of auditions and "a whole series of workshops" before the filmmakers decided to go with Brodie-Sangster."I didn't get it in the end, obviously," he added, "but I do remember meeting Hugh Grant and Richard Curtis and sitting down and reading some scenes."

5. Colin Firth played Jamie, a writer who leaves London for his French country home after learning his girlfriend cheated on him with his brother. There, Jamie meets Portuguese housekeeper Aurélia (Lúcia Moniz). And while they don't speak the same language, they understand the feelings they've formed for each other.Jamie returns to England for a family Christmas party only to turn back around and, after learning some Portugese, propose to Aurélia. As he leaves, his niece yells, "I hate Uncle Jamie." And apparently, the name was a playful jab at Curtis' brother."Richard only called colin firth's character 'jamie' so the kids could say 'I hate uncle jamie,'" his wife and script writer Emma Freud tweeted in 2015. "His brother is called jamie."6. As for Aurélia, Curtis shared in the director's commentary the name was a nod to a friend-slash-employee who looked after his and Emma's son.7. In one scene, Jamie types outside while Aurélia clears a cup that had been holding down his papers, resulting in the wind sweeping them into a lake. Curtis said they used a wind machine so loud the lines were dubbed.Aurélia dives in to retrieve the pages, and Jamie follows. However, Curtis said the lake was only 18 inches deep at the time of filming."They're kneeling now, pretending to swim, but actually crawling along the bottom, the poor things," he added in the commentary. "And Colin got stung by a sort of animal and his elbow swelled up to the size of three avocados the next day."

8. Martine McCutcheon played Natalie. Her character joins the staff of the newly elected prime minster David (Grant), and the two develop a crush on each other.Curtis knew McCutcheon was the one for the role right from the get-go."I wrote Martine McCutcheon's part for her, too," he told The Guardian. "I even called the character Martine, though I had to change it before the read-through so she didn't think she'd already got it."

9. One of Grant's most famous scenes is when he does a celebratory dance to The Pointer Sisters' song "Jump (For My Love)" after standing up to the U.S. president. However, the actor wasn't thrilled about having to bust out some moves."I think I saw it in the script," Grant said in 2022 for The Laughter & Secrets of Love Actually: 20 Years Later – A Diane Sawyer Special, "and I thought, 'Well I'll hate doing that.'"In fact, Curtis said Grant "kept saying no." Still, the Notting Hill star gave in eventually."He was grumpy," Curtis added in the special. "It was a contractual obligation, a bit of contractual obligation acting."As for his reaction to Grant's performance in that scene?"I’m thinking, ‘Oh, good he’s doing it,'" he recalled. "Two, that’s agonizingly embarrassing.”And Grant admits he was off with his lip-synching and dancing."I'm out of rhythm by the way," he told Diane Sawyer, "especially at the beginning when I wiggle my ass.”However, Grant is willing to take a bow for the scene's ending."It was my idea to have the secretary lady catch me," he noted in the special. "Genius!"

10. While it's clear Laura Linney's character Sarah had a crush on her co-worker Karl (Rodrigo Santoro), it wasn't as obvious to viewers that the costars were navigating their own heartaches off-screen."Hands down, I got the best kiss. Sorry!" the actress said on a 2019 episode of The Graham Norton Show, referencing Sarah and Karl's make-out session that ends when she receives a call about her brother Michael's mental health battle and leaves to be with him. "And it was sweet because we were both very brokenhearted when we made that movie. He had just been dumped, I had just been dumped."Linney recalled how she and Santoro were "slumped in the van" lamenting about their breakups while on their way to film the scene."I turned to him, and I said, 'Well all day long we get to make each other feel better,'" she remembered, "and I think there is a sweetness to the scene because of that. We were both very sad."

11. Fans certainly said "I do" to the scene where Keira Knightley's charater Juliet marries Chiwetel Ejiofor's Peter, especially the part where the couple walks down the aisle and are surprised by musicians popping up from the church pews to perform The Beatles' "All You Need Is Love."While the wedding is a joyful part of the film, the inspiration for it actually came from a day of mourning: Jim Henson's funeral, which Curtis called "the most moving thing" he's ever attended."At the end of it, Frank Oz was talking and he suddenly lifted up Kermit's puppet and started to sing this song called 'One Voice,'" he explained in the director's commentary. "And it turned out all the guys in the memorial service had brought their puppets with them, and they lifted them up. And when you turned around and looked backwards, there were 50 puppets all singing. And Big Bird walked down the aisle of St. Paul's Cathedral, and they all came forward and just this massive chorus of puppets all singing. It was an extraordinary thing. So, this was our little stab at that."

12. After the wedding, Juliet visits Peter's best friend Mark (Andrew Lincoln) to see if he captured any video footage of the wedding day. While she was under the impression he hated her, she learns (after popping in a VHS tape featuring footage of only her at the wedding) that he's actually been shielding his romantic feelings for her. In the scene, Juliet wears a hat. However, Knightley explained there was a reason for this fashion choice.

“I got the biggest zit of my life when we were shooting this scene,” the actress told Jimmy Fallon on a 2019 episode of The Tonight Show. “And this scene is the important one, isn’t it? It was like another head growing out of my head."While Knightley said the makeup and lighting departments tried to hide the pimple, it was no use."There was nothing they could do," the Pride & Prejudice star added, "so the hat went on."

13. Fast-forward to later in the movie, Mark shows up at Juliet and Peter's house and rings the door bell. When she answers, he instructs her to tell her husband it's carol singers. Mark then comes clean about his love for her through a series of cards, including one that says "To me, you are perfect." In fact, Lincoln actually wrote out the cards himself.

"It is my handwriting!" The Walking Dead actor told Entertainment Weekly in 2013. "It’s funny, because the art department did it, and then I said, 'Well, can I do it?' because I like to think that my handwriting is really good. Actually, it ended up with me having to sort of trace over the art department’s, so it is my handwriting, but with a sort of pencil stencil underneath."Juliet and Mark then part ways after she gives him a controversial kiss goodbye. In a 2017 sequel short for Red Nose Day, it's revealed that Juliet and Peter are still married and that Mark has tied the knot with supermodel Kate Moss, who was featured on one of his cards in the OG film.

And that wasn't the only notable memory from shooting the romantic moment. Knightley also recalled having to redo her reaction to his cue card reveal a few times so that the gesture seemed less "stalker-ish."

In a December 2024 interview withVariety, she detailed changing up her facial expression to try to improve the scene, saying she wound up “having to redo it to fix my face to make him seem not creepy.”

14. While there appears to be a bigger age gap between Knightley and Brodie-Sangster in the movie, they're only five years apart IRL. She was 17 when they made the film, and he was 12.

15. Brodie-Sangster really did learn how to play the drums for Love Actually, in which his character picks up the instrument to impress his crush Joanna (Olivia Olson) at their school's Christmas concert."I did learn to play the drums for it,” he told The Sunday Post in 2017. “My dad’s a drummer and he taught me in my grandad’s basement bashing away on his old kit and trying to play along to 'All I Want For Christmas [Is You].'”16. And yes, that really was Olson singing the Mariah Carey hit."Everyone thinks she is lip-synching, and she was 9 or 10 years old," screenwriter Freud said at the Montclair Film Festival in 2016, per the event's recap of her presentation, "but that was her.”17. What's more, the scene where Joanna gives Sam a peck on the cheek at London's Heathrow Airport before she flies back to America marked her first on- and off-screen kiss.

"I was really nervous because I kind of had a crush on Thomas back in the day," the actress told E! News in 2016, "and I was also worried because I was taller than him."The kiss clearly left an impression on both characters. In the 2017 Red Nose Day special, it's revealed that Sam reconnected with Joanna in New York and that they got engaged—with them flying back to London to ask Neeson's character Daniel for his blessing.

18. Another unforgettable scene is when the character Harry (played by the late Alan Rickman) is trying to buy a necklace for his secretary Mia (Heike Makatsch) without his wife Karen (Emma Thompson) knowing, but the jewelry salesman Rufus (Rowan Atkinson) is moving at a snail's pace.And apparently, the Mr. Bean star was in no rush to finish filming the scene.

20. One of the most heartbreaking parts of the movie is when Karen finds the necklace in Harry's coat pocket, thinks it for her and then unwraps a Joni Mitchell CD for Christmas instead—leading her to realize he bought the necklace for another woman.After she puts on a smile for their children's Christmas concert, Karen tells Harry she knows what's going on. And while fans wondered if the couple remained married, Freud solved this mystery. "They stay together," she tweeted in 2015, "but home isn't as happy as it once was."And Freud says Harry's relationship with Mia went beyond the necklace."DEFINITELY had an affair," she wrote, "i begged richard just to make it a flirtation, but no. the whole way."

21. With several other beloved rom-coms under his belt—including Four Weddings and a Funeral, Notting Hill and Bridget Jones's Diary—Curtis resurfaced a scene he'd cut in a previous film for Love Actually.The scene stars a man named Colin (Kris Marshall), who is serving hors d'oeuvres at a wedding. In a failed attempt to flirt, he strikes up a conversation with a woman and tells her how bad the food is—except it turns out the woman is the caterer."This highly amusing scene coming up now about catering with this girl is a re-working of a highly amusing scene about catering, which bore remarkable resemblance down to the last line which was originally in Four Weddings and a Funeral," Grant, who appeared in both films, revealed while doing the director's commentary with Curtis, "which was one of my audition scenes, but which got cut from the final film."In fact, Curtis admitted he forgot to change the name from Charles in Four Weddings and a Funeral to Colin in Love Actually in a line of the re-worked script.22. Fed up with searching for love in the U.K., Colin decides to go to America and try his luck there. He flies to Wisconsin, where he meets a group of women at a bar, including one named Jeannie played by January Jones."January jones wrote half of her lines," Freud revealed in a tweet. "She was sooooo funny when we filmed that scene."

23. While there were several familiar faces in Love Actually, Freud revealed her and Curtis' kids also made a few cameos."THAT IS SCARLETT CURTIS THERE ON THE RIGHT," she tweeted about her daughter, who was dressed as one of the lobsters in the school's Nativity play (yes, you read that right). "NOT EVEN JOKING."In addition, she noted the boy with the crown and Spider-Man face-paint in the Christmas play is their son Jake, with her writing, "I gave birth to him."24. Looking back at the film two decades later, Curtis admits there are aspects of the film he wishes he could change."The lack of diversity makes me feel uncomfortable and a bit stupid," he admitted in the Diane Sawyer special. "I think there are three plots that have bosses and people who work for them."The director has also expressed regret over the film's comments about Natalie's weight.“I think I was behind, you know, behind the curve, and those jokes aren’t any longer funny," he told The Hollywood Reporter in 2023, "so I don’t feel I was malicious at the time, but I think I was unobservant and not as, you know, as clever as I should have been.”

25. While Love Actually features 10 different storylines, Curtis said he originally had more.

"At first, we had 14 different love stories, but the result was too long, so four ended up going, including two we'd actually shot," he told The Guardian. "One was based on a poster in Alan Rickman's office of two women in Africa. The camera actually went into the poster and heard them talking about their daughters' love lives. Another involved Emma Thompson's son getting into trouble at school and the camera following the harsh headmistress home."In the since-released deleted scenes, the headmistress can be seen heading home to take care of her partner Geraldine, who is dealing with an illness and later dies. Another deleted scene shows Sarah talking about family Christmas memories with her brother Michael. They ask each other how they're doing now. While Sarah says "everything's great," Michael gets real with her about his mental health struggles and says, "I'm in hell."Even though Curtis decreased the number of storylines, he admitted stringing the remaining ones together was no easy feat.

"Although all the strands come together in the airport at the end, it still felt like making 10 separate films," he told The Guardian. "It was a massively difficult edit. The order I originally wrote it in didn't work at all, so we had to reorder it completely. It was a bizarre four-month game of 3D chess."

#868. Carrick's Man Utd future to be decided as Berrada and Wilcox retain support

Michael Carrick arrived at Manchester United's training ground on Tuesday

Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick's future will be decided at a meeting on Wednesday attended by owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, who remains supportive of executives Omar Berrada and Jason Wilcox.

Carrick's position is under threat after the club slipped to 18th in the Premier League following a chaotic 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford on Sunday.

Minority owner Ratcliffe, chief executive Berrada and director of football Wilcox will meet in Monaco to decide the 45-year-old's future.

BBC Sport reported on Monday there was a growing expectation Berrada and Wilcox would recommend to Ratcliffe and majority owners, the Glazer family, that Carrick be sacked.

They will present their recommendation, although the Glazers will also be consulted, and a decision on the manager's future may not be announced until Thursday.

BBC Sport also understands at this stage Ratcliffe remains supportive of Berrada and Wilcox, despite mounting criticism of the pair from fans.

Berrada and Wilcox recommended Carrick be appointed permanent head coach in May after an impressive spell as interim boss.

Wednesday's meeting in Monaco, which is where Ratcliffe is based, was already planned and has not been organised to strictly discuss Carrick's future.

However, that will form part of the talks, which could also include whether to bolster his coaching team.

If the decision to sack Carrick is made at the meeting, the club want to inform him face to face. He is said to understand that United's form has made discussions over his future inevitable.

United have made their worst start to a domestic campaign in 40 years, but the hierarchy still believe a top-five finish is possible.

The Monaco summit that will decide the future of Carrick and Man Utd

BBC Sport reported in October United had sounded out former Newcastle boss Eddie Howe and ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann about replacing Carrick.

Former Chelsea coach Antonio Conte is known to be keen on the role, while multiple sources have told BBC Sport former Spurs boss Mauricio Pochettino is open to a move to Old Trafford.

Pochettino signed an extension to his contract as USA coach in August.

However, the deal is thought to contain clauses that would allow him to leave for specific high-profile jobs. The US have a two-legged Concacaf Nations League play-off with Haiti on 14 and 18 November.

Man Utd score twice in stoppage-time to share points in eight-goal thriller

Pochettino, Howe, Emery... or Carrick? Man Utd's managerial options

The draw with Villa was Carrick's third match in charge since the club opted to give the 45-year-old more time at Old Trafford.

Results during that time - a win, a draw and a defeat - were mixed, and displayed the best and worst of Carrick's reign with United shipping goals but displaying good character to come back from two goals down on three occasions.

United's board toyed with sacking Carrick after the loss to Bournemouth, but decided the Englishman - and his players - had earned the opportunity to show that they could turn the club's fortunes around.

It was also felt that the two-week international break in November represented a better chance for the club to properly assess the club's start to the campaign.

Unfortunately for Carrick, it makes for poor reading.

With one victory in 10 Premier League matches, United have made their worst start to a top-flight campaign since the 1986-87 season.

They sit 18th in the table, one point above bottom-placed Crystal Palace.

Only the Eagles and Ipswich have conceded more than the 19 goals United have shipped in the Premier League this season.

It is hard to believe given the club's current predicament just how quickly Carrick's tenure has soured.

Four 'huge mistakes' that show Man Utd's defensive problems

Looking back, the 48 hours before United's season-opening match at Hull were pivotal.

With Benjamin Sesko still trying to ease his way back from the shin issue that ended his previous campaign early, Amad Diallo suffered an ankle injury that would rule him out for seven weeks. It meant Carrick was deprived of his first-choice striking alternative, with Bryan Mbeumo having to play on the right of the attack.

Carrick instead turned to Matheus Cunha, whose preference for dropping deep took him into the spaces captain Bruno Fernandes likes to occupy.

It neutralised United's attack on a day they seemed ill-prepared to meet the physical challenge of an opponent motivated by their long-awaited Premier League return.

In his role as interviewer for Nordic broadcaster Viaplay, former Norway and Middlesbrough striker Jan Aage Fjortoft later claimed United had lacked passion - something Carrick dismissed as "ridiculous".

"It's one game," Carrick told the media afterwards.

The following week, United were losing to Ipswich - another newly promoted side. Only a slip from Marcelino Nunez inside his own half allowed Cunha to tee up Fernandes for an undeserved equaliser.

The Portugal playmaker, who had just been crowned PFA Player of the Year for 2025-26, went on to complete a hat-trick in a 5-2 win.

He has scored just once - a penalty against Villa on Sunday - in the league since.

After the Ipswich win came a trip to Everton.

Twice United led, the second occasion when Sesko struck two minutes from full-time after coming on as a substitute. Deep into stoppage time, Ainsley Maitland-Niles drove home from long range to deny the visitors.

Asked how confident he was in his side's ability to react to a disappointing start to the season, Carrick snapped back: "It's not been that bad."

Time and again, United's fitness was called into question. They struggled badly against a Manchester City side reduced to 10 men in the first half before their rivals benefited from an Erling Haaland goal that referees' chief Howard Webb later admitted should not have stood.

Carrick's complaints were justified - but they masked a poor performance from his team.

After taking a 2-0 lead inside 10 minutes against Brighton in the EFL Cup, United were outplayed and beaten, thanks to two goals in four second-half minutes.

The fine margins United benefited from during Carrick's interim spell were now going against them, and his coaching staff - lauded months earlier - could not find an answer.

Carrick called Cunha's injury-time equaliser against a Fulham side who started the game bottom of the table a positive to build on. But immediately after the international break, United were held to another draw - conceding in injury time to an out-of-form and 10-man Tottenham.

The whirlwind was starting to pick up strength.

Lisandro Martinez, who scored an own goal against Fulham, was at fault for Spurs' leveller, which made his post-match outburst after the 2-0 Champions League defeat by Atletico Madrid more amazing.

The Argentina defender criticised United's summer recruitment and placed the blame at the door of "the technical director" - Wilcox.

By the time of Martinez's outburst, Sesko and left-back Luke Shaw were injured. Marcus Rashford has not played since. The rotation at left-back that eventually led to Carrick starting five different players in that role was in full swing.

After conceding in the opening minute against Atletico, Como scored inside the first two in a 4-1 Champions League defeat for United. Fernandes came out afterwards and criticised Carrick's tactics.

He was dropped for the Bournemouth game, but returned as captain at Chelsea. United were beaten in both matches.

With just three wins in 15 matches in all competitions this season and United stuck in 18th in the Premier League, Carrick is set to pay the price.

Spotted a dazzling light in the eastern sky before sunrise? It's Venus, and the planet is only going to get brighter as it heads toward its spectacular peak later this month.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!"

The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence.

On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come!

In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight.

It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky.

In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew.

After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition.

So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight.

Joe Rao serves as an instructor and guest lecturer at New York's Hayden Planetarium. He writes about astronomy for Natural History magazine, Sky and Telescope, The Old Farmer's Almanac and other publications.

#865. Who are the main candidates for the Aberdeen job?

Steven Pressley, John McGlynn and Steve Clarke have all been mentioned in despatches

Another season, another managerial sacking at Aberdeen.

Stephen Robinson's departure on Monday made it five dismissals since the spring of 2021.

The Northern Irishman followed Stephen Glass, Jim Goodwin, Barry Robson and Jimmy Thelin in making an abrupt exit on the watch of chairman Dave Cormack.

Most of the quintet have lasted less than a year and, although Thelin ended the Dons' 35-year wait to win the Scottish Cup, the general trend has been one of perceived underachievement in Scottish Premiership.

Derek McInnes, now with Rangers after spells at Kilmarnock and Heart of Midlothian, was the last Pittodrie boss to regularly deliver consistent results in the top flight and consequent European qualification.

So who could be next? And what qualities does such a manager require?

'Aberdeen hunt yet another manager after ill-fated Robinson reign'

Aberdeen sack Robinson after league slump

Falkirk add goals and grit to McGlynn's guile on rapid rise

Two names mentioned fairly early on after Robinson's exit were Dundee's Steven Pressley and Falkirk's John McGlynn.

Both have impressed in the Premiership this past 17 months, drawing admirers for style of play and good results.

Falkirk are third in the division, two places above Dundee, and McGlynn's side were sixth last season, again two places higher than Pressley's men.

Former Aberdeen defender Richard Foster said the pair are "the two that stand out for me domestically" and said of Elgin-born Pressley on BBC Radio Scotland's Breakfast: "I know he's got a quiet, laid-back demeanour, but I think in the dressing room, he commands respect.

"The players at Dundee seem to love playing for him.

"He knows the game very well. Having played at Hearts, having played at Celtic, he knows what it's like to be at a huge club."

Former Hearts, Hibernian and Scotland midfielder Michael Stewart has been impressed with McGlynn's track record of signing players.

Speaking on McGlynn on BBC Radio Scotland's Sportsound, Stewart said: "John McGlynn puts the miles in.

"He's up and down the road down south. He's up and around all over Scotland. He knows what the players are that are perhaps not in the eye of many others. He knows them intimately before they arrive at Falkirk.

"So it's no great surprise that his success rate with recruitment is pretty, pretty good.

"I would not be surprised if, whenever one or two of the bigger jobs start coming up... rather than being sort of an outsider, I think he'll be right in the hunt for some of those jobs."

Former Celtic and Hibs midfielder Scott Allan says McGlynn is "very tactically astute" and commented: "I love everything that John McGlynn does. Everybody in Scottish football can respect the job he's done there, the consistency.

"He's one of the most prepared managers, if not the most prepared manager for any sort of set-up that he faces week-to-week and he's shown that.

"It's a fantastic job he's done over the last three or four years. He deserves all the credit that comes his way."

It may seem like a lifetime ago, but it's actually only been five months since Steve Clarke stepped down as Scotland head coach.

The 63-year-old, like McGlynn, has vast coaching experience, including in Scotland after a two-year spell with Kilmarnock.

Clarke oversaw three qualifications to major tournaments with Scotland, ending long waits to appear at the European Championship and World Cup.

As well as managerial stints at West Bromwich Albion and Reading, Clarke has worked at Chelsea, Liverpool and Newcastle United, so little would daunt the former right-back.

Appointing Clarke would be a statement by Aberdeen and the challenge of restoring the club to competitiveness may be a compelling one for the man himself.

However, along with McGlynn, geography may play a part and their candidacy could depend on whether personal circumstances allow a switch to the north east.

Wigan Athletic boss and former Scotland centre-half Gary Caldwell has also been linked with the Pittodrie job. The 44-year-old cut his managerial teeth with the Latics and returned there earlier this year after spells in charge of Chesterfield, Partick Thistle and Exeter City.

Swede Thelin stands out as one of the few overseas managers Aberdeen have had.

Yes, Goodwin and Robinson hail from Ireland and Northern Ireland respectively, but both are very much embedded in Scottish football after spending so much time at various clubs north of the border.

The only other non-Scottish manager to grace the Pittodrie home dugout was the Dane, Ebbe Skovdahl, from 1999-2002.

As such, it is fair to say Aberdeen have not experimented too much with foreign coaches and have tended to go with faces familiar to the Scottish top flight.

With a German, Lutz Pfannenstiel, as the sporting director, Aberdeen look further afield this time?

It has become the vogue in the Premiership of late, with Hearts, Hibs and Motherwell going foreign, with Belgian Wouter Vrancken, Dutchman Marink Reedijk and Swede Alfred Johansson in recent months.

Should Pfannenstiel unearth the next Jens Berthel Askou, formerly of Motherwell, Dons fans will be delighted.

Podcast: What is going wrong at Aberdeen?

https://www.bbc.co.uk/sounds/play/p0pm7gkd

Former Aberdeen defender Stuart Duff is in interim charge of Aberdeen following the departures of Robinson, assistant Brian Kerr and coach Stephen Craigan.

The Dons are second bottom of the Premiership, two points above Kilmarnock.

Unless an appointment is made during the international break, Duff faces taking Aberdeen to face Kilmarnock on 21 November before visiting Rangers three days later, with their next home game being against Dundee on 28 November.

Confidence is low after seven league defeats so far this season, but the tightly-packed middle section of the league means Aberdeen are only a couple of wins off the top six.

#864. How Aspyn Ovard's Throuple With Married Couple Plays Out on SLOMW: OC

Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County star Aspyn Ovard exclusively told E! why she feels the truth about her relationship with married couple Bri and Billy Davis will take viewers by surprise.

And the influencer did exactly that by taking fans inside her relationship with married couple Bri Davis and Billy Davis while filming The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives: Orange County.

"There's a lot of different arcs of my life that are shared on the show," Aspyn exclusively told E! News. "But I am excited to be representation of a different kind of relationship."

And there's a reason the 30-year-old looks forward to viewers getting a look at her life in a throuple on Hulu’s Secret Lives of Mormon Wives spinoff, premiering Nov. 12.

As she put it, "Because there's just not a lot out there, and it's easy to share for me. And I know it's not easy for everybody."

Though the YouTuber—who filed for divorce from ex Parker Ferris in 2024 after eight years of marriage—admitted exploring the new chapter of her sexuality was "a big deal" for her, fans shouldn't expect any major plot twists while witnessing her current relationship.

"I'm very curious to kind of see what people will say because I think that I've seen some crazy theories, and it's just not that crazy of a thing," Aspyn, who began sharing about her bisexuality online following her breakup with her high school sweetheart, noted with a laugh. "I think unfortunately people will be a little bit underwhelmed."

Still, the mom of three girls—Cove, 7, Lola, 5 and Elle, 2—clarified, "It was very overwhelming for me."

Ahead of Mormon Wives: OC's release, Aspyn and Bri detailed how their love story came together—including how Aspyn signaling her queer identity led to Bri reaching out.

So, when the TikToker suggested, "What if we all hung out?" referencing the nurse's husband, Bri was open to expanding their connection.

"I was like, 'I’m not opposed.' I already really like you, and I knew her vibe and her energy, and I knew Billy’s vibe and energy," Bri explained in their Oct. 11 YouTube diary. "I was like, 'They kind of match.' Like, I kind of—I can see the vision."

Despite ongoing relationship speculation, Salomé Andrea and Aaron Brimhall are still going strong as they prepare to welcome their third baby together. The duo, who married in 2012, also share 8-year-old twins Luca and Rue.

McCall DaPron—the sister of Mormon Wives' Mayci Neeley—shares four kids with husband Kirk DaPron, who she wed in 2011.

Ashleigh Pease and Nate Pease are rock solid after over a decade of marriage. "This 13th year together is one that has felt full circle!" she wrote on Instagram in September. "A season of fruits. Comfort. The happiest milestones."

#863. Felix Nmecha denies goal celebrations promote ‘intolerance, discrimination and hate’

Celebrations linked to ultra-conservative Christian group

‘Our message is of love’ Nmecha says in reply to criticism

The Borussia Dortmund and Germany midfielder Felix Nmecha has responded to criticism of goal celebrations linked to an evangelical network by saying they have been misunderstood and are not meant to promote “intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form”.

Nmecha, a devout Christian, was criticised by the Dortmund official supporters’ group at the weekend for celebrating goals with a gesture signifying the “The King’s Return” campaign linked to Ballers in God (BIG), a network of Christian football players. The German public broadcaster ARD has linked BIG to ultra-conservative positions on issues including homosexuality and transgender identity.

“My celebration is not intended to promote myself or any organisation,” Nmecha wrote in a social media post on Tuesday. “Rather, it is about laying my ‘crown’ before the soon coming King and pointing to Jesus, my hope and strength. My message has never been about promoting intolerance, discrimination, or hate in any form.

“As Christians, our message is one of love and respect for everyone, regardless of where they come from, what they believe, or what their worldview may be.”

In a statement, Dortmund official supporters’ group said: “We oppose religious networks that, under the guise of faith, propagate a worldview in which individuals are denigrated or excluded based on their sexual orientation, gender identity, way of life, or personal choices”.

Dortmund said on Sunday that it understood the fans’ concerns and would speak to Nmecha. “For Borussia Dortmund, it is essential to take the concerns and needs of the fanbase seriously and to address them,” read a statement. “Naturally, we also take the current media coverage and the associated questions and discussions very seriously.”

The news agency DPA reported that Jürgen Klopp, Germany’s head coach, has already spoken to Nmecha about the issue at the national team camp in Herzogenaurach, Bavaria, before the upcoming Nations League games.

#862. Kompany back at Bayern training after collapse

Head coach Vincent Kompany has returned to Bayern Munich's training ground after collapsing at the end of last month.

The 40-year-old former Manchester City captain was taken to hospital after falling ill while watching the club's second team train.

Kompany was diagnosed with meningeal irritation - an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord.

Bayern said in a statement: "Vincent Kompany is on the road to recovery and has been back at the training ground since the start of the week."

However, the Bundesliga leaders did not hold a training session, with most players away on international duty.

English coach Aaron Danks has been in charge during Kompany's absence, leading Bayern to four victories and a draw.

They face Cologne next on 20 November after the end of the two-week international break.

Kendall Jenner and Jacob Elordi are keeping it cozy.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Another new private rocket is in the works.

AST SpaceMobile announced today (Nov. 6) that it's building a reusable rocket called Blacklift to launch its broadband satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO), with first flight targeted in 2028.

The news comes just 10 days after Cowboy Space unveiled Big Iron, a rocket designed to launch its constellation of 20,000 AI data centers. Cowboy Space is also targeting 2028 for its first liftoff.

"The Blacklift rocket is the springboard to significantly expand our total addressable market, providing AST SpaceMobile with regular unconstrained access to orbit and providing for most favorable owners’ economics in the industry," Abel Avellan, the company's founder, chairman and CEO, said in a statement today.

"This will accelerate our mission to build a new layer of global connectivity, extending connectivity beyond terrestrial networks and helping to bring AI-enabled services wherever people live, work and travel," Avellan added.

Texas-based AST SpaceMobile is building a LEO constellation composed of its BlueBird satellites, which beam internet service directly to cell phones. The company has launched 13 BlueBirds to date, including eight "Block 2" variants. The antennas on each of these next-gen spacecraft cover a whopping 2,400 square feet (223 square m) — the largest ever deployed in LEO by a commercial satellite.

BlueBirds have flown atop three different rockets to date — SpaceX's Falcon 9, Blue Origin's New Glenn and India's Launch Vehicle Mark-3. But AST SpaceMobile wants to get more vertically integrated, which explains the push to develop Blacklift.

The company won't be starting from scratch. It has signed a deal with another Texas-based outfit, Firefly Aerospace, to provide the engines (and associated engineering services) for the first three Blacklift launches. After that, AST SpaceMobile will build the engines itself, under a licensing agreement with Firefly.

Those engines are Miranda, which will power Blacklift's booster, and Vira, which will power the upper stage.

Neither engine has flight experience. (Firefly's currently operational rocket, Alpha, uses Reavers in its booster and Lightnings in its upper stage.) But Miranda has been tested extensively on the ground, firing for more than 4,200 seconds over the course of 175 hot fires, according to AST SpaceMobile.

"The Miranda engine will allow us to leapfrog the traditional five-to-10-year development cycle as we build Blacklift," AST SpaceMobile President Scott Wisniewski said in the same statement.

The "supply and services" agreement for the first three launches is worth $500 million. The licensing agreement cost AST SpaceMobile about $800 million, with half of that paid in cash and half in stock, according to the statement.

Blacklift will be able to haul 20 tons to LEO. Each launch will therefore be able to loft up to five BlueBird satellites, according to today's announcement. (For perspective: The Falcon 9's LEO lift capacity is about 25 tons.)

BlueBirds will continue going up while AST SpaceMobile gets Blacklift ready to fly: The company already holds contracts with other providers to launch more than 100 of the satellites over the course of 2027 and 2028.

The launch landscape will likely be very different when Blacklift, Big Iron and other new rockets come online. SpaceX has said that it plans to phase out the Falcon 9, as well as its Falcon Heavy heavy lifter, after its Starship megarocket gets up and running.

That milestone could come in the next few years, ushering in something of a launch crunch for satellite operators. SpaceX has indicated that it will prioritize launches of its own satellites with Starship. And there will be a lot of them to loft — 100,000 Starlink V3 satellites and a million Starmind AI data centers, company founder and CEO Elon Musk has suggested.

#859. Mongolia’s iconic grasslands are in crisis — invisible fungi could help save them

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

April Reese is a journalist in Aveiro, Portugal.

More than 70% of Mongolia’s land is degraded, which has implications for the country’s nomadic herders.Credit: Timothy Allen/Getty

Rising temperatures, desertification and overgrazing are taking a heavy toll on Mongolia’s iconic desert grasslands, as well as its nomadic herding culture. But a team of researchers might have hit on an underground solution. They’ve found clues that protecting key fungal networks that support life above the surface could help to preserve biodiversity, boost climate resilience and revive degraded lands.

In most ecosystems, invisible networks of fungi trade resources with plants by interlocking with their roots. These arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi provide the plants with nitrogen and phosphorus gathered from the soil; in return, the plants send excess carbon through their roots to the fungi, helping to sequester it from the atmosphere.

“Mongolia has very unique fungal networks that power these arid grasslands,” says evolutionary biologist Toby Kiers at the Free University of Amsterdam. Kiers is leading a project to map and identify mycorrhizal-fungus hotspots in Mongolia. “As we fight desertification, we want to be able to protect the fungi that are going to be so important for these plants and ecosystems to be restored.”

Working out ways to maintain healthy fungal networks cannot come quickly enough. Around 77% of Mongolia’s land is degraded, and the country is warming three times faster than the global average. Kiers says that paying more attention to fungal networks could help to address the interconnected global challenges of desertification, biodiversity loss and climate change.

It seems that fungi might be starting to get the attention they deserve: last month, at the latest meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Convention on Biological Diversity, held in Yerevan, Armenia, 3 more countries signed a pledge to conserve fungi, bringing the total number of signatories to 17. And a road map to help countries make good on that pledge, the Global Strategy for Fungal Conservation, was launched.

Kiers’s team is part of the Society for the Protection of Underground Networks (SPUN), a non-profit organization that maps fungal systems around the world and works to protect them. Kiers co-founded the organization in 2021. In September, its researchers announced that they had found more than 500 types of fungus in southwestern Mongolia, 90% of which were previously unknown.

Kiers’s team is in talks with several governments to present its maps of fungal hotspots and data in hopes of supporting the development of strategies to curb desertification and boost climate resilience.

But at the same time as researchers such as Kiers are documenting fungal hotspots, the hotspots might be disappearing. In Mongolia, the team found that degraded land had at least 44% fewer species of mycorrhizal fungi and 60% less plant cover than did non-degraded land.

doi: https://doi.org/10.1038/d41586-026-03589-9

#858. Leicester and Brentford U21 into EFL Trophy knockout stages

Will Smallbone's strike proved to be the winner for Leicester City against Walsall

Brentford U21 and League One side Leicester City both moved into the knockout stages of the Jersey Mike's Trophy with vital victories.

The Bees had to beat the Football League's basement side Crawley Town in their final fixture in Southern Group H to progress and did so courtesy of a Domeiro Bobb-Semple double in a 2-1 success at Broadfield Stadium, where Connor Wickham scored on his Crawley debut.

In Southern Group B, the Foxes trailed at the King Power Stadium against League Two Walsall, who would have gone through in place of their hosts with a win. But strikes from Will Smallbone and John Lundstram put them ahead by the break and they held on.

Stevenage topped the group by beating Fulham U21 on penalties.

Chelsea U21 were not in action but went through at the expense of Reading, who needed a big win away against Bristol Rovers to see them overtake the west London side in Southern Group C, but the Royals were beaten on penalties.

Nottingham Forest U21 and Notts County both eased through into the last 16 with wins in Northern Group F.

Forest enjoyed a 3-0 success against League Two promotion-chasers Grimsby Town at Blundell Park, where all the goals came before the break.

The Magpies moved into the knockout stages as group winners by beating League One Burton Albion by the same scoreline for a third win in three EFL Trophy games.

Domeiro Bobb-Semple (right) scored a goal in each half for the Bees youngsters

In Southern Group F, Leyton Orient needed a big victory over Barnet to claim an unlikely second-placed finish on goal difference, but they were well beaten at The Hive, with Jack Maskell's first-half strike setting the hosts on the way to a 4-2 win.

Oxford United coasted to a 4-0 win over Cheltenham Town to go second in Southern Group A - and will stay there as long as they avoid a heavy defeat against Tottenham Hotspur U21 in their final fixture.

In Southern Group G, Gillingham made sure of their place in the last 32 by seeing off Northampton Town 2-1. The Gills only needed a point to be certain of finishing in second place above Brighton & Hove Albion U21, but Lamin Sillah scored one goal and made another to inspire his side to victory over their League Two rivals.

Seb Campbell crashed home a 99th-minute winner as Plymouth Argyle beat Swindon Town at Home Park to finish top of the pile in Southern Group E, while Colchester United beat Ipswich Town U21 on penalties after a 0-0 draw in Southern Group D, in a match where both sides knew their campaign had ended after their second fixture.

Elsewhere, a close-range shot by Tom Graves put Crewe Alexandra on track for the win they needed to progress from Northern Group B, but Wigan Athletic scored twice in the second half to dash their hopes, while veteran forward Nick Powell was among the scorers as Bradford City thumped York City 4-0 to top Northern Group C.

In a thriller in Northern Group D, already eliminated Mansfield Town looked set for their first points of the competition as they led already qualified Chesterfield 3-1 with 28 minutes remaining. But Dylan Duffy scored two of four goals in the closing stages to earn the Spireites a remarkable 5-3 victory.

Stockport County beat Tranmere Rovers on penalties in Northern Group E, but both sides were already sure of qualification, while Huddersfield Town thumped Liverpool U21 4-0 to finish top of Northern Group H.

#857. Rui Pinto’s lawyers in talks with UK authorities over deal for Manchester City whistleblower

He is willing to assist in exchange for protection

Rui Pinto’s lawyers are in talks with British authorities over a potential cooperation agreement under which the Manchester City whistleblower could help to expose serious financial and sporting crime in the UK.

According to information obtained by the Guardian, the Serious Fraud Office has contacted Pinto after it emerged he was willing to assist British authorities with their investigations in exchange for protection.

William Bourdon, Pinto’s lawyer, who has represented whistleblowers such as Edward Snowden and Julian Assange, told the Guardian that contact had been established. “I can confirm that the process is under way,” he said, without providing further details.

If an agreement is reached, the Football Leaks founder could become a significant source of information in investigations into financial crime involving football, law firms and powerful business figures. Between 2015 and 2019, Pinto collected tens of millions of files containing sensitive information. He may be able to assist the SFO in identifying potential tax offences and other irregularities that would otherwise have gone undetected.

The development comes at a significant moment for the 38-year-old Pinto, with his future under Portugal’s witness protection programme uncertain.

Pinto rose to prominence by exposing some of the football industry’s most closely guarded secrets. These included Cristiano Ronaldo’s tax affairs, plans by Europe’s leading clubs to establish a breakaway European Super League and a series of controversial financial arrangements. His revelations triggered investigations and contributed to legal proceedings involving clubs and players across several countries.

More recently, documents collected and leaked by the whistleblower became relevant to the Premier League’s investigation into Manchester City, which resulted in the club being found in breach of financial rules.

The information gathered by Pinto is in the possession of French authorities, who sought previously to include him in a witness protection programme. His arrest by Portuguese police in Hungary in January 2019 disrupted those plans, although France has maintained contact with him. Between his arrest in Hungary and his extradition to Portugal, French authorities travelled to Budapest and copied the contents of the electronic devices in his possession.

Pinto was informed on 30 September, just as his name had made headlines again after the City ruling, that he would no longer be protected by the Portuguese authorities after six years under the witness protection programme. Although the authorities maintained there was no threat to his life, he was advised not to express opinions on controversial issues, to avoid crowded places and to limit the time spent with family members.

The best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s action

Pinto was given 10 days’ warning, even though a decision had been taken in July, and the ruling’s implementation was suspended after it was established that he had not been given an opportunity to mount a challenge or appeal. He then appealed and is awaiting a final ruling.

In 2023 Pinto was given a suspended four-year prison sentence in Portugal for attempted extortion and cybercrime offences. He was acquitted in a second case involving similar charges two years later. The public prosecutor’s office and Benfica, one of the clubs hacked by Pinto, appealed against the ruling. A decision from the higher court is awaited.

Supporters regard Pinto as a whistleblower who cast light on corruption, whereas detractors argue that his tactics breached legal standards and moral principles. His disclosures reached far beyond football. Details involving magistrates, legal professionals and public officials were made public and he was the whistleblower behind Luanda Leaks, which exposed the inner workings of the business empire of Africa’s richest woman, Isabel dos Santos. She denied corruption allegations.

#856. Love Is Blind's Michaella Giorgio Clarifies Matt the Beekeeper Romance

Love is Blind alum Michaella Giorgio shared new insight into her brief romance with beekeeper Matt Waldrip after their awkward reaction during the season 11 reunion.

Not all of Michaella Giorgio’s Love is Blind memories are sweet like honey.

In addition to her onscreen turmoil with then-fiancé Rob Feeley, the show’s season 11 reunion confirmed Michaella and beekeeper Matt Waldrip gave their connection a shot after filming—though the reveal came with a sting.

Now, Michaella, 35, is sharing additional insight into the awkward interaction, including why she had such a heated reaction to Matt saying he’d fallen in love with her.

“It was a hurtful conversation because what he chose to say publicly was incredibly different from what we discussed privately,” she told Glamour in an interview published Nov. 9. “He did end his relationship with me because he said he wasn’t in love with me, so I don’t understand him now coming to the reunion—another person I haven’t talked to since November of last year—and saying all of those things, and then saying he was there for me.”

As she put it, “I was very taken off guard and annoyed because it’s just not true.”

According to the fashion professional, she and Matt, 37, first tested their connection for a couple weeks right after filming in the spring of 2025, before Michaella felt she was “not even remotely close to being ready to date” and ended things.

“Then we tried again last October and broke up,” she said. “He came over my house and broke up with me on Thanksgiving eve.”

She confirmed that, yes, the reason he gave for their split was that he wasn’t in love with her.

Nevertheless, during the reunion—which aired on Nov. 8—Matt told Michaella, “Ultimately, I did fall in love with you during that time, and I'm sorry that I'm the one that ended it. I genuinely wish you all the happiness and success in the world.”

But when he called her a “queen” and began to say that if she ever needed anything, he’d be there, Michaella abruptly cut him off.

“I need nothing,” she said. “I need nothing. I need nothing. Newsflash, nothing.”

She also shared the POV from her side of the beehive.

“Matt and I had a really great friendship that shouldn't have crossed friendship,” she explained. "I think that's definitely an exaggeration of our relationship. We dated for a few weeks, and I dropped you off at your mom's house and met your mother. I don't think we were in love.”

And when Matt stressed their time had been “meaningful” to him, and that he felt sorry she didn’t remember it the same way, she further dampened his buzz.

“I did say I love you, but I did not say I was in love with you,” she admitted, before adding. “We're going to be transparent: I was on mushrooms, which you knew that I took.”

Michaella and Matt’s connection is just one of the many now-failed relationships to have emerged from season 11 of Love is Blind. Read on for more LIB updates.

On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day.

Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star."

At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it.

The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572, is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star.

While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky.

"The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia, was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004. "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova."

"This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time.

Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis, or the Blaze Star, the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so.

Hanneke Weitering is a multimedia journalist in the Pacific Northwest reporting on the future of aviation at FutureFlight.aero and Aviation International News and was previously the Editor for Spaceflight and Astronomy news here at Space.com. As an editor with over 10 years of experience in science journalism she has previously written for Scholastic Classroom Magazines, MedPage Today and The Joint Institute for Computational Sciences at Oak Ridge National Laboratory. After studying physics at the University of Tennessee in her hometown of Knoxville, she earned her graduate degree in Science, Health and Environmental Reporting (SHERP) from New York University. Hanneke joined the Space.com team in 2016 as a staff writer and producer, covering topics including spaceflight and astronomy. She currently lives in Seattle, home of the Space Needle, with her cat and two snakes. In her spare time, Hanneke enjoys exploring the Rocky Mountains, basking in nature and looking for dark skies to gaze at the cosmos.
